articles.title: 263 Forgotten Recipes: NIPS Kolkata Cooks Up a Culinary World Record
articles.excerpt: In a six-hour marathon on September 10, 126 students at Kolkata's NIPS Institute of Hotel Management prepared 263 rare and forgotten Indian recipes — provisionally adjudicated by the World Book of Records London.
articles.image_caption: NIPS Kolkata faculty and chefs hold the World Book of Records certificate at the record event. The institute's students prepared 263 forgotten regional recipes over six hours for 'Rare Cuisines of India — From Kashmir to Kanyakumari.'

sources.label: Travel and Tour World — NIPS Revives 263 Rare and Forgotten Indian Recipes
Devdiscourse — NIPS Hotel Management Institute Sets Record with Largest Diverse Dessert Spread

articles.nri_angle: Diaspora kitchens already act as quiet archives of the regional recipes NIPS documented, and this project offers families abroad a model — and a reference — for recording disappearing dishes before the last people who know them are gone.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gymkhana Dubai Opens: London's Two-Michelin-Star Indian Restaurant Hits DIFC
articles.excerpt: The two-Michelin-starred London institution from JKS Restaurants has opened its first UAE outpost in DIFC's Gate Village, pairing Mayfair signatures with its largest set of location-exclusive dishes yet.
articles.image_caption: The opulent dining room at Gymkhana's Dubai outpost, with crystal chandeliers, tiger artwork and a peacock-motif bar. The two-Michelin-starred London restaurant opened its 137-seat DIFC location on September 1, 2026.

sources.label: Pantime Arabia — Gymkhana Arrives in Dubai
Time Out Dubai — Gymkhana is opening in Dubai soon

articles.nri_angle: Gymkhana's Dubai debut plants a British-Indian Michelin success story in a Gulf city where Indians are a huge share of the population, showing Indian fine dining is now judged in Dubai as much as in London.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's food prices set to rise further as El Niño weakens monsoon, economists warn
articles.excerpt: With August retail inflation at a 20-month high of 4.82% and the monsoon deficit the worst since FY16, economists warn food-price pressures could keep inflation above 5% and force the RBI's hand.
articles.image_caption: Wheat being harvested in India. An erratic monsoon and El Niño conditions are pushing up food prices, with retail inflation at 4.82% in August, a 20-month high.
articles.nri_angle: Rising food prices hit diaspora families supporting relatives in India, and RBI rate moves shape the rupee and Indian markets that NRI investors watch.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Very Hot Beverages Linked To Triple Esophageal Cancer Risk, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A study of nearly a million UK adults found those who prefer drinks 'very hot' face more than triple the risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — but researchers stress it's the heat, not the chai, that matters.
articles.image_caption: Two steaming mugs of a hot beverage. A study of nearly a million UK adults found that preferring drinks 'very hot' more than triples the risk of esophageal cancer.
articles.nri_angle: Indian households serve chai boiling and order it 'kadak,' but the science says the drink is innocent and the scalding is not — diaspora chai drinkers can keep the ritual and simply let the cup cool a few minutes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Haryana Seizes 7,500 Kg of Suspected Fake Paneer Bound for Delhi Markets
articles.excerpt: Food safety teams raided four unlicensed dairies in Haryana's Nuh district, confiscating thousands of kilos of synthetic paneer laced with vegetable oils, starches and detergent residue before it reached Delhi markets.
articles.image_caption: Cubes of white paneer on a wooden cutting board. Food safety officials in Haryana’s Nuh district have seized about 7,500 kg of suspected adulterated paneer from four unlicensed dairies, part of India’s widening crackdown on synthetic dairy.
articles.nri_angle: NRI visitors should be cautious about paneer served through bulk catering and restaurant supply chains in the Delhi NCR, where synthetic product from illicit dairies has been circulating; the broader FSSAI warning-label push also matters to diaspora shoppers of Indian packaged foods abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Paneer Lababdar, Millet Pulao and Mulberry Phirni: What BRICS Leaders Ate at Modi's Gala Dinner
articles.excerpt: A ten-course vegetarian banquet at Bharat Mandapam took world leaders from Gujarati khandvi to Himalayan morels to mulberry-topped phirni — with millets front and centre.
articles.image_caption: BRICS leaders, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, seated at the gala dinner at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The menu highlighted millet-based dishes and regional Indian ingredients, including paneer lababdar and mulberry phirni.
articles.nri_angle: The gala dinner menu showcases regional Indian cuisine on the world stage, a point of cultural pride for the diaspora, and continues India's millet diplomacy that diaspora food writers have been tracking since 2023.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Healthy' Snacks May Not Be: What a Nutritionist Says About Millet Chips, Ragi Cookies and Makhana
articles.excerpt: Nutritionist Lakshmi Kale tells Hindustan Times' 'Indian Food Decoded' that processing, oil and salt can undo the benefits of millet, ragi and vegetable ingredients in packaged snacks.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of Indian namkeen mixture at a snack shop. Nutritionist Lakshmi Kale says millet chips, ragi cookies and makhana should be judged as finished products rather than by a single wholesome ingredient on the label.
articles.nri_angle: Indian grocery stores and mainstream supermarkets alike are full of millet chips and makhana marketed to health-conscious Indian families — the same label-reading discipline applies wherever you shop.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sanjeev Kapoor's Pineapple Sheera: A Step-by-Step Guide to the Festive Dessert
articles.excerpt: The celebrity chef's fruity take on the classic semolina dessert combines roasted rawa, ghee and fresh pineapple — a simple, festive sweet that takes about an hour.
articles.image_caption: Pineapple sheera served in a bowl, garnished with nuts. Celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor shared the recipe for the festive semolina dessert ahead of the festival season.
articles.nri_angle: A classic Indian dessert many in the diaspora grew up with gets a fresh twist — an easy, familiar recipe for festive gatherings abroad, using ingredients available in any Indian grocery store.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zomato Starts Charging Up to Rs 20 on Cash-on-Delivery Orders
articles.excerpt: The 'pay on delivery fee' appears as a separate line in the bill summary on cash orders, on top of platform fees, packaging charges and GST — while online payments remain exempt.
articles.image_caption: A Zomato app bill summary shows the new "Pay on delivery fee" of Rs 5 on a cash-on-delivery order. The fee, which can range up to Rs 20, began appearing on orders from September 12.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs ordering food for family back in India — and anyone watching India's delivery duopoly — now see another line item on the bill, with cash-paying customers bearing the cost.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Table for One: Are Indian Restaurants Ready for the Solo Diner?
articles.excerpt: A quiet cultural shift is emptying the stigma from eating alone in India, as restaurants redesign seating, menus, and service for guests of one.
articles.image_caption: A person eats alone at a restaurant table. Solo dining is on the rise in urban India, and restaurants are redesigning their spaces for parties of one.
articles.nri_angle: The solo-dining wave mirrors what Indian buffet restaurants in the US already see, and it changes what NRIs visiting India can expect: the corner table is no longer the loneliest seat in the house.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Telangana Bans Artificial Non-Dairy Paneer for One Year After Raids
articles.excerpt: The state's food safety authority prohibited analogue paneer sold as "paneer" from September 10, 2026, and suspended five FSSAI licences in Hyderabad after enforcement drives found unhygienic conditions and adulterated ingredients.
articles.image_caption: Seized bags labelled cheese analogue are piled up during a food safety enforcement drive in Telangana. The state has banned the manufacture and sale of non-dairy analogue paneer sold as paneer for one year from September 10, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora shoppers are reminded to check paneer ingredient labels abroad — genuine paneer lists milk and an acidulant, while substitutes rely on vegetable oils and emulsifiers — and families visiting Telangana will find restaurant paneer under closer scrutiny.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Crispy Corn: How to Make the Restaurant-Style Spicy Snack at Home
articles.excerpt: Golden, spice-dusted sweet corn kernels with a shattering crunch — here is how to nail the Indian restaurant starter at home, plus the details that keep it crisp.
articles.image_caption: Crispy corn tossed in chaat masala and chilli. The Indo-Chinese starter is made by deep-frying cornflour-coated kernels at 175 to 180 degrees Celsius.
articles.nri_angle: A beloved Indian restaurant starter that home cooks in the US can make with pantry spices and grocery-store corn; note that Indian cornflour is sold as white cornstarch in American stores.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Modak Became Lord Ganesha's Favourite Sweet, According to Mythology
articles.excerpt: From a divine contest on Mount Kailash to the ritual offering of 21 modaks, the sweet's bond with the elephant-headed god runs through myth, wisdom and devotion.
articles.image_caption: Modaks prepared for naivedyam. Devotees customarily offer 21 modaks to Lord Ganesha during Ganesh Chaturthi.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American families keep the modak tradition alive at Ganesh Chaturthi, using the sweet and its myth as a way to pass cultural memory to the next generation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Nalli Nihari to Lotus Mithais: How Delhi Is Feeding the BRICS Summit
articles.excerpt: The Taj Mahal, New Delhi spent months researching delegate preferences to build an 'India Friendship Menu' for the 18th BRICS Summit — and every delegate goes home with a recipe book.
articles.image_caption: Gulab jamuns soaked in sugar syrup. Delhi's kitchens are feeding the BRICS summit with a menu running from nalli nihari to lotus mithais.
articles.nri_angle: The summit's culinary showcase highlights how Indian regional cuisine is now presented as soft power to world leaders — a source of pride for the diaspora watching from abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja Food Waste to Power Civic Hospitals During Ganeshotsav
articles.excerpt: Under BMC's 'Prasad to Power' plan, 8–10 tonnes of wet waste from Mumbai's most famous Ganesh pandal will be converted into electricity for municipal hospitals across the 11-day festival.
articles.image_caption: Mumbai's Lalbaugcha Raja Ganesh idol. Food waste collected during the festival will power civic hospitals.
articles.nri_angle: The initiative pairs faith with sustainability at one of the diaspora's most-watched festivals, giving NRIs who follow Ganeshotsav from Mumbai's celebrations a tangible example of Indian cities linking devotion to environmental responsibility.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Microlot coffee: Inside India's limited-edition world of specialty brews
articles.excerpt: From Tata Coffee's Nullore Estate at the Starbucks Reserve Roastery to yeast-washed lots from Ratnagiri, India's microlots — tiny, experimental, estate-separated batches — are winning global awards and selling out in small runs.
articles.image_caption: Freshly roasted specialty coffee beans. India's microlot scene is bringing limited-edition brews from estates in Coorg and Chikmagalur to urban cafes.
articles.nri_angle: Indian specialty coffees are increasingly available through online roasters and premium cafes abroad, giving diaspora drinkers a traceable, estate-level cup from Coorg and Chikmagalur.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: MasterChef's Jyoti Vishnani on Building an Indian Kitchen Under ₹10,000
articles.excerpt: The MasterChef India Season 4 contestant says a great Indian kitchen comes down to ingredients, technique and wisely chosen tools — not expensive gadgets.
articles.image_caption: Chef Jyoti Vishnani in her kitchen. The MasterChef contestant shares how to build an Indian kitchen for under ₹10,000.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs setting up first kitchens abroad can build the same starter kit — pressure cooker, kadhai, tawa, masala dabba — for a fraction of a month's eating-out budget.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Which Roti Wins on Protein, Fibre, Iron and Calcium? Nutritionist's Answer
articles.excerpt: Nutritionist Kiran Kukreja's comparison finds ragi leads on calcium, amaranth on protein and bajra on magnesium — but her real advice is to rotate grains, not abandon wheat.
articles.image_caption: Rotis served with onion chutney. A nutritionist breaks down which roti wins on protein, fibre, iron and calcium.
articles.nri_angle: Every one of these flours — ragi, jowar, bajra, makki, rajgira — is stocked in Indian grocery stores across the US and Canada, usually at prices close to wheat atta.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Atta Halwa: The Grainy, Ghee-Rich Whole-Wheat Dessert You Can Make in 25 Minutes
articles.excerpt: A simple 1:1:1 ratio of flour, ghee and sugar — plus slow roasting and a warm syrup — delivers the danedar, juicy halwa of gurdwara fame, no lumps.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of atta halwa garnished with slivered almonds. The grainy, ghee-rich whole-wheat dessert comes together in about 25 minutes.
articles.nri_angle: Atta halwa uses only ingredients available in any American grocery store, making it one of the most practical Indian desserts for diaspora kitchens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lindt Opens Its First-Ever India Store in New Delhi's Aerocity
articles.excerpt: The Swiss chocolatier's 1,100 sq ft Worldmark boutique features a 25-flavour LINDOR Pick & Mix bar, live chocolatiers and festive gifting ranges — a first for the brand in India.
articles.image_caption: A flat-lay shows Lindt LINDOR truffles and a red gift box. Lindt & Söprüngli opened its first India store at Worldmark, Aerocity, New Delhi, on September 4.
articles.nri_angle: A beloved international brand the diaspora grew up buying abroad is now a destination for visitors home — with a gifting angle timed for the Diwali season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'I Won't Eat From Your Hands': Kerala Chef's Reply to Skin-Tone Troll Goes Viral
articles.excerpt: Chef Karthikeyan answered a troll who mocked his skin tone by listing the prominent guests he has served — a calm rebuttal that turned colourist abuse into a conversation about dignity.
articles.nri_angle: Colourism travels with the diaspora, showing up in casting, workplaces and South Asian grocery aisles abroad; the chef's calm, factual rebuttal resonates across borders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: In Bengal, Non-Veg Is Not a Treat During Durga Puja — It Is Bhog
articles.excerpt: For Bengali families, mutton and hilsa offered to the Goddess on Navami are sacred prasad — a Shakta tradition that stands apart from North India's vegetarian Navratri.
articles.image_caption: Bhoga served during Durga Puja in West Bengal, where non-vegetarian offerings like mutton are part of the feast.
articles.nri_angle: Bengali-American families reassemble this tradition every autumn at community pujas and Bengali groceries, where khichuri bhog and Navami mutton keep the Shakta meaning of the festival alive abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sri Lankan-Style Coconut Kheema: A Creamy 350-Calorie Weeknight Dinner Fix
articles.excerpt: Nutritionist-chef Aathira Sethumadhavan's recipe borrows from Sri Lanka's coconut gravies and Kerala's moilee and mappas, packing 22g of protein into a one-pan chicken kheema dinner with mushrooms and spinach.
articles.image_caption: Coconut kheema with mushroom and spinach, served with flatbread. The Sri Lankan-style dish is a 350-calorie weeknight dinner.
articles.nri_angle: A 22g-protein one-pan dinner that fits busy Indian-American weeknights, fusing Sri Lankan coconut-gravy technique with pantry staples most diaspora kitchens already have.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sabudana Kheer: The Creamy Fasting Dessert That Needs No Soaking
articles.excerpt: This translucent tapioca-pearl kheer is a Navratri and vrat staple, but it works as an everyday dessert too — and a no-soak method cooks the pearls directly in water before the milk goes in.
articles.image_caption: A bowl of sabudana kheer, the creamy tapioca-pearl dessert eaten during fasting days.
articles.nri_angle: Tapioca pearls are stocked in nearly every Indian grocery in the US, and the no-soak method lets busy diaspora families make this Navratri bhog on a workday evening without planning ahead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How to Make Restaurant-Style Curry at Home, According to Indian Chefs
articles.excerpt: From browning onions patiently to finishing with a tadka, professional chefs explain the techniques that separate restaurant gravy from homemade versions.
articles.image_caption: A restaurant-style Indian curry. Professional chefs say patience and layered technique are the keys to replicating restaurant flavors at home.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora home cooks working with limited time, even applying two or three of these techniques can noticeably close the gap between weeknight cooking and restaurant quality.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Inside Bollywood Producer Jackky Bhagnani's Wholesome Weekly Meal Plan
articles.excerpt: From neer dosa with chicken curry to yakhani pulao with raita, the producer shows that eating healthy doesn't have to mean eating boring.
articles.image_caption: Bollywood producer Jackky Bhagnani shared his weekly meal plan on Instagram, featuring dishes from stuffed chicken with pesto to yakhani pulao with raita.
articles.nri_angle: Bhagnani's mix of South Indian, Mughlai, and pan-Indian meals offers a practical template for diaspora families balancing health and traditional flavours.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
